title: The Silent Call Bell
subtitle: You and I both know that the bell signals the start of the show.

items.text: The Silent Call Bell

items.speaker: Cavalry
items.text: Hurry! Don't let them slip away!
A swift squad of knights races through the streets, their torches illuminating the night.

items.speaker: Cavalry
items.text: Stay indoors, everyone! Not one step out!

items.speaker: Cavalry
items.text: This time, we will catch them!
The clash of metal armor and loud commands echoed through the streets.
The town square, in the heart of the city, was in disarray, with no one to be seen.
Until the distant bells chimed.
As if declaring or beckoning:
Come one, come all.
At the far end of the street, a clown with exaggerated makeup appeared, clutching a torch.

items.speaker: The Fool
items.text: Congratulations! You've captured us poor souls, who've suffered so unjustly.

items.speaker: Cavalry
items.text: You...you're that outlaw from the wanted posters!

items.speaker: The Fool
items.text: Wanted?

items.speaker: The Fool
items.text: What a laugh! Who gives meaning to those useless scraps of paper?

items.speaker: Cavalry
items.text: They are the Duke's command! No one dares disobey!

items.speaker: Charlie
items.text: And who gave him the power to give these commands?
A performer in elegant attire emerged on the opposite side of the street, coolly observing the multitude of knights.

items.speaker: Cavalry
items.text: What nonsense are you spouting?

items.speaker: Charlie
items.text: Why, it's the people.

items.speaker: Charlie
items.text: They gave him that power.

items.speaker: Charlie
items.text: But then he violated their trust, and he lost the power they gave him.

items.speaker: Charlie
items.text: And tyrants quake at its happening—

items.speaker: Charlie
items.text: Just as King John feared Arthur, Claudius feared Hamlet, and Macbeth feared Malcolm.

items.speaker: Charlie
items.text: The usurper fears the true wielder of his power.

items.speaker: Charlie
items.text: He fears us—fears the true holders of that power.

items.speaker: Cavalry
items.text: Enough! Stop this deceitful talk! Seize them all!

items.speaker: Charlie
items.text: But first, let us savor our final act.
Once more, the distant bells rang out.

items.speaker: Charlie
items.text: That is your cue, Mr. Fool.

items.speaker: The Fool
items.text: As you wish.
The clown raised his torch and flung it aside.
Flames swiftly spread from the torch to the buildings lining both sides of the street.
The fire escalated rapidly, transforming the street into an impassable wall of flames.

items.speaker: Cavalry
items.text: What are you doing... have you all lost your minds?!

items.speaker: Cavalry
items.text: Quick! On my mark, turn back and retreat!

items.speaker: Soldier
items.text: Captain! The way back is blocked!
The cavalry captain turned in shock.
Suddenly, a large crowd gathered around Charlie.
Silent and unmoving, they stood like an impenetrable wall.

items.speaker: Charlie
items.text: You thugs, did I not warn you? This is the final act—but not ours, yours.

items.speaker: Charlie
items.text: Savor your last gasp of fear, for on its tail quickly comes...the anger of the people!

items.speaker: Soldier
items.text: Captain! There's nobody on the other side of the street. We can break through there!

items.speaker: Soldier
items.text: Wait...are they forcing us to break through ahead?

items.speaker: Cavalry
items.text: These blasted troublemakers...

items.speaker: Soldier
items.text: I see it now!

items.speaker: Soldier
items.text: They fear the Duke's might!

items.speaker: Soldier
items.text: They won't dare kill us! They fear the Duke's retaliation, so they're forcing us out through another gate!

items.speaker: Cavalry
items.text: What a despicable lot, daring to turn against their betters!

items.speaker: Soldier
items.text: Captain, if we don't run now, it'll be too late!
As the fear heightened the cavalry leader seemed to remember something.

items.speaker: Cavalry
items.text: No, no! I won't fall for this!
A confident smile spread across his face.

items.speaker: Cavalry
items.text: Hah, your performance was compelling. It almost fooled me!

items.speaker: Cavalry
items.text: But alas, arcanist, your act lacked a certain spark.

items.speaker: Charlie
items.text: What are you babbling on about, you up-jumped stable boy!

items.speaker: Cavalry
items.text: I've heard of you and your arcane illusions. This is all your trick, isn't it?

items.speaker: Charlie
items.text: An interesting conclusion...

items.speaker: Cavalry
items.text: Hah, these flames, this crowd... They are mere illusions you created!

items.speaker: Cavalry
items.text: You're just making a blustering show of bravado, but your nothing more than fools!
Despite delivering a pinnacle performance, Charlie's expression momentarily wavered.
The cavalryman revealed a smug smile, convinced he'd spotted his adversary's weakness.

items.speaker: Charlie
items.text: See for yourself whether it's real or an illusion.

items.speaker: Cavalry
items.text: Still want to play the braggadocio, eh? Get her!

items.speaker: Cavalry
items.text: You dare to resist the Duke's power with cheap illusions...

items.speaker: Cavalry
items.text: Honestly, your actions are as laughable as your sorcery.

items.speaker: Cavalry
items.text: Get her! Take her away!
Suddenly, the bells chimed again, but this time, they sounded unusually long, ringing out a different tune.
The echoes of the bells faded, replaced by a different sound.
The sound of footsteps.
A vast thunder of steps approached from all directions, and soon, flickering torchlights dotted every alley of the street.
With this new crowd converged behind Charlie.

items.speaker: Jeffrey
items.text: Stop! I am Jeffrey from the City Council!

items.speaker: Jeffrey
items.text: Your actions are hereby condemned by the Council! On behalf of the City Council of Autonoma, we order you to leave now!

items.speaker: Charlie
items.text: What's this...?!

items.speaker: Cavalry
items.text: City Council?! Do you even know who we are?!

items.speaker: Old Man
items.text: Nothing more than henchmen of a tyrant, get out!

items.speaker: Vendor
items.text: You're not welcome here!

items.speaker: Resident
items.text: Leave! Leave now!
As the furious crowd gathered behind Charlie, the flames on both sides of the street roared higher.
The temperature rose, and beads of sweat formed on the henchmens' foreheads.

items.speaker: Soldier
items.text: C-Captain, t-this doesn't look like an illusion anymore!

items.speaker: Soldier
items.text: I've never heard of any arcanist creating something like this...

items.speaker: Cavalry
items.text: It's all an illusion, you cowards! Here, let me show you...
The captain of the cavalry gritted his teeth and charged into the burning flames.

items.speaker: Cavalry
items.text: Damn it! It's scorching! It's- it's real fire?!

items.speaker: Charlie
items.text: Indeed! And it burns with the people's rage.

items.speaker: Charlie
items.text: And should you trample on the people, then they'll reclaim their power.

items.speaker: Charlie
items.text: That which rightfully belongs with them.

items.speaker: Charlie
items.text: Respect a just ruler, but ever resist a tyrant—

items.speaker: Charlie
items.text: This is the reckoning of the people.

items.speaker: Charlie
items.text: Still think these angry crowds are just an illusion?

items.speaker: Cavalry
items.text: You dare—
The cavalryman's words were cut off by a rotten egg thrown from the crowd.
Though it bounced harmlessly from his heavy armor, the humiliation pierced him deeper than any bolt or arrow.

items.speaker: Charlie
items.text: Still think this is just a trick?
The bells...
The bells rang louder and more fervently.
They sounded like they were urging a final judgment.
The captain's spirit finally crumbled.

items.speaker: Cavalry
items.text: Madmen... a bunch of madmen!

items.speaker: Cavalry
items.text: How dare you rabble defy the Duke's—
His muttered words were consumed by the crowd's condemnation.

items.speaker: Charlie
items.text: Don't say I didn't warn you. Leave now while you still can.

items.speaker: Charlie
items.text: ...Or face the fury of the people.
She raised a hand, and the crowd parted, creating a path behind her.

items.speaker: Cavalry
items.text: Damn it... let's go... let's go! Retreat, retreat!
The soldiers meekly sheathed their weapons and retreated towards the city gate.

items.speaker: Old Man
items.text: That's it! Don't show your faces here again!
Laughter erupted among the crowd.
The soldiers' arrogance had given way to dejection, in stark contrast to their previous bravado.
TO BE CONTINUED ...
